name: Bluebell

waypoints.name: Lake Serene Trailhead (Trail #1068)
waypoints.directions: From US 2 about 7 miles east of Gold Bar (near milepost 35), just as the highway curves left toward the bridge over the Skykomish River, turn right (south) onto Mount Index Road. Follow the gravel road about a quarter mile, turn right at the sign for Lake Serene Trail 1068, and park in the lot about 500 ft ahead at roughly 600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required.

approach: From the Lake Serene Trailhead (~600 ft) off Mount Index Road, follow the maintained Lake Serene Trail — roughly 3.6-4.1 miles (accounts vary slightly) and about 2,000 ft of gain, passing the Bridal Veil Falls spur around mile 1.6 and switchbacking up to Lake Serene (~2,600 ft). At the lake, leave the maintained trail for the unofficial climbers' path that traverses talus and large boulders around the west side of the lake; in early summer this crosses avalanche debris and lingering snow/ice at the lake's edge. Continue up talus beneath the imposing north/east face of North Index toward the cirque below the Norwegian Buttresses, then work up through the brushy base of the wall — steepening mossy slabs and brush that some parties rope up for before reaching clean rock on the buttress proper. Reliable water is available at Lake Serene and its outlet creek, but not higher on the talus approach, so fill up at the lake. Plan roughly 2-3 hours from the trailhead to the base of the wall, more with a loaded pack for a multi-day ascent.
